purpose: Legal reference matrix for independent original homebrew, spiritual successors, interoperability, platform hardware and retro evolution. Statements describe potential rules, not automated legal conclusions.

NO.label: Norway
NO.note: Norway applies its Copyright Act and EEA-implemented provisions; do not assume an EU case alone settles a Norwegian hardware circumvention case.

EU_EEA.label: EU/EEA (national implementation must also be checked)
EU_EEA.note: Domestic law and contractual, trademark, design, patent and consumer rules may apply alongside EU harmonized copyright.

US.label: United States
US.note: Check both exclusive rights and anti-circumvention separately; exemptions often narrow and are not general commercial distribution permissions.

OTHER.label: Other or unverified jurisdiction
OTHER.note: No global safe-harbor assumption; require jurisdiction-specific qualified review.

authorities.title: Åndsverkloven § 41 — use of computer programs
principles: observation / testing while lawfully using copy
authorities.caution: Does not itself license copied expressive game materials or general-purpose circumvention.

authorities.title: Åndsverkloven § 42 — reverse engineering for interoperability
authorities.caution: Limited conditional exception; a generic remake or market replacement is not automatically eligible.

authorities.title: Åndsverkloven § 99–100 — technical protection of works
authorities.caution: Some audiovisual game protection may differ from program-specific treatment; analyse the specific measures and legal uses.

authorities.title: Åndsverkloven § 101 — technical measures protecting software
authorities.caution: Not a general permission to market bypass tools.

authorities.title: Directive 2009/24/EC Arts. 1, 4–7 (software copyright)
principles: ideas and principles excluded from program copyright
authorities.caution: Program exceptions do not erase audiovisual, artistic, musical or trademark rights.

authorities.title: Directive 2001/29/EC Art. 6 (technological measures)
authorities.caution: Hardware restrictions and TPM challenges require concrete proportionality/jurisdiction review.

authorities.title: C-406/10 SAS Institute v World Programming (2012)
authorities.caution: Not a license to copy game art, dialogue, code, sound or distinctive audiovisual look.

authorities.title: C-355/12 Nintendo v PC Box (2014)
authorities.caution: Do not interpret as blanket authorization to circumvent consoles, distribute bypass devices, or pirate games.

authorities.title: U.S. Copyright Office — Games
principles: game ideas and methods not themselves copyrightable
authorities.caution: Original audiovisual assets, narrative and expressive look and feel remain relevant.

authorities.title: 17 U.S.C. § 1201 — technological measures
authorities.caution: A copyright-noninfringing game does not automatically make TPM bypass legal.

authorities.title: U.S. Copyright Office 2024 § 1201 exemptions
authorities.caution: Preservation exemptions do not generally confer commercial remake, distribution, or piracy rights; current cycle must be checked.

authorities.title: Tetris Holding v Xio Interactive, 863 F.Supp.2d 394 (D.N.J. 2012)
principles: unprotected gameplay idea vs protectable artistic implementation
authorities.caution: Even when code is independently written, copied expressive look and feel may infringe.
